name: Hydrangea Red
lede: Hydrangea Red is a muted, greyed red, the color of the flower heads when they take on a reddish tone.

sections.title: Named for a changeable flower
sections.body:
Paterson lists hydrangea pink as a yellowy pink, with hydrangea blue and hydrangea red as variants [1]. The names recognise that the same bush can flower in different colors. The books read give no more than that, so the name's first coiner is undocumented [1].

The swatch enters the atlases early: Ridgway's 1912 atlas (plate XXVII), the 1930 Maerz and Paul dictionary and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system, which calls it grayish red [2]. Japanese traditional color lists give a near twin, *ume-nezumi*, the grey of plum [2]. Neighbors are [[red]], [[rose]] and [[old-rose]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The color is moderately common in paintings: 243 of 23,781, about 1.0 per cent [3]. It is mostly an accent, and it peaks in the 1900s at 2.1 times the expected rate [3]. A match from the year 1000 is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of a dye [3].
